correctness.rationale: For n=2k+1, split the boundary at the opposite-side midpoint into two reflected arcs. On each edge V_jV_{j+1} for 0≤j≤k−1, the squared-distance derivative has the displayed nonnegative/positive trigonometric form and strict convexity makes distance strictly increasing; on V_kM it strictly decreases by quadratic symmetry. Hence each radius occurs at most twice per arc and at most four times globally. Radii between V_0M and V_0V_k occur exactly twice on each arc. The published all-boundary four-intersection statement gives the matching lower bound.

value.rationale: Regular odd polygons are explicitly singled out in the foundational paper as the canonical family disproving Erdős’s original bound 2. Determining their exact invariant closes that natural benchmark family: the lower bound was known, while the new argument gives a sharp uniform upper bound and a complete open interval of radii with exactly four intersections at every vertex.
